title: Implementation and evaluation of mobile health tools for personalised follow-up of patients in radiation therapy for prostate cancer
summary:
Over the past few years, mobile health-apps have received increasing attention in health care and health care research. They are hoped to contribute to improving processes and outcomes of health care. 
Also, they are expected to facilitate patients' involvement in their own care and to adapting care to the individual patient's needs. 

The present study therefore aims at developing, implementing and testing the use of an app that allows patients with prostate cancer under radiation therapy to record their therapy-related preferences and quality of life ratings while receiving therapy and follow-up care and to also share their experience with their physician when wishing to do so. Based on these data, relationships between therapy-related preferences and psychosocial distress as well as quality of life will also be explored.

interventions.name: Patients with prostate cancer who recieve either an intensity-modulated radiation therapy (IMRT) or brachytherapy (HDR)

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
SUBSTUDY 1: 
Prostate cancer patients under radiation with curative intent, 
histologically proven PCA,
cT1-3,
cN0, cM0,
Gleason Score 6-9,
PSA <40 ng/ml.

SUBSTUDY 2: 
Patients with primary prostate cancer of favorable-intermediate- to very-high risk after NCCN (National Comprehensive Cancer Network)
histologically proven PCA,
cT2a-3b (MRT, PET/CT),
cN0 und cM0 (MRT, PET/CT),
Gleason-Score 7-9,
ECOG Performance Status  0 or 1,
IPSS < 15,
size of prostate ≤ 75 ml (as of date of radiation therapy planning)
Exclusion criteria:
SUBSTUDIES 1 and 2: insufficient command of German language, patient too much distressed by his condition, acute psychosis, risk of suicide present.
